Where it began

Justin Langer was born in Perth on 21 November 1970 and went to school at Newman College and Aquinas College, which later named a shield after him for their year-seven pupils to play for. Cricket ran in the family: his uncle Rob Langer was a left-handed batsman for Western Australia in the 1970s and 1980s.

He played for the state's junior sides and Australia under-19s, won a place at the Australian Cricket Academy in 1990 and was in the Western Australia team by 1991–92.

The player

His Test debut came against the West Indies at Adelaide in January 1993. The first ball he faced, from Ian Bishop, hit him on the head. He made 54 in the second innings all the same, the top score in a famous chase that Australia lost by two runs. For some years after that he came and went from the side, and his first Test hundred arrived only in October 1998, at Peshawar.

The turn came in 2001, when he moved up to open with Matthew Hayden at The Oval and marked the move with a century. By the time Langer finished, at Sydney in January 2007, only Gordon Greenidge and Desmond Haynes had made more Test runs together as a pair. In 105 Tests he scored 7,696 runs at 45.27, with 23 hundreds and a best of 250 against England at Melbourne in December 2002.

What made him special

Langer was a fighter. At Hobart in 1999 he and Adam Gilchrist came together at 126 for 5, chasing 369 against Pakistan, and put on 238 to win the match. At Perth in 2004 he made 191 and 97 against Pakistan, outscoring their whole team in both innings. In 2009 he passed Sir Donald Bradman as Australia's leading first-class run-scorer, and his 342 for Somerset in 2006 was the biggest innings anyone had played for the county.

He was not built for one-day cricket, at least in the selectors' eyes: just eight ODIs, all between 1994 and 1997, despite piles of runs in the domestic competition. And he bowled in a Test exactly once, a single over at Kolkata in 2001, when Steve Waugh had tried almost everyone else.

Away from the middle

He was a Wisden Cricketer of the Year and a Member of the Order of Australia. He went on to coach Western Australia, the Perth Scorchers and, from 2018 to 2022, Australia, whom he led to the T20 World Cup title in 2021. In July 2023 he took over at the Lucknow Super Giants. He is the author of several books, among them The Power of Passion and Keeping My Head, and he earned a probationary black belt in the martial art of Zen Do Kai.

And finally

Ian Bishop, the bowler who greeted him with that first ball in 1993, went on to become a close friend. A Melbourne band, Telemachus Brown, wrote a song about him in 2006, (Wrong about) Justin Langer. The title may have been a nod to how his career turned around. His 23 Test hundreds made that point more firmly.
